sentences.text:
Shri A.K. Saraswat, learned counsel for the Petitioner.
 Shri Kshitij Vyas, learned Panel Lawyer for the responden Heard on I.A. No.12043/2024, which is an application under Section 438(2) of BNSS, 2023 (Section 397(1) of CrPC) for suspension of sentence of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail, filed on behalf of the petitioner.

2. The petitioner has been convicted under Sections 16(1)(A)(I)(II) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to undergo 1 year R.I., with fine of Rs.5000/- and usual default stipulations.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the Court below has not properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record and committed error in convicting the applicant.
The applicant has suffered one month in custody out of total sentence of one year R.I.
This revision would take considerable to dispose of finally.
There are so many contradictions and omissions in the prosecution witnesses.
Looking to the short sentence learned counsel prays that the application for suspension of sentence of the petitioner be allowed.
6. Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the application for suspension of sentence.

7. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, contention of learned counsel for the petitioner, without commenting on the merits of the 2 CRR-3731-2024 case, the application is allowed and it is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if already not deposited, the petitioner shall be released on bail, on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of Trial Court, for his appearance before the Registry of this Court firstly on 25.11.2024 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard, till final disposal of this revision.
